1. Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes — reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% relative to recent history.

2. Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends — adjust downward bias by adding 2–5% of the recent 7-day average to forecast.

3. Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days — apply a 1-day smoothing filter or use 7-day moving average to align with actual price momentum.

4. After a price spike, model overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot — cap forecast at 1.2x the peak price within 3 days to prevent excessive overcorrection.

5. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.

6. Forecast is overly sensitive to recent volatility — dampen forecast response to 3-day moving average of historical volatility to avoid erratic swings.
